role: Transparency by sampling a render of the scene behind the mesh at the pixel's screen position (FBO).
adaptation: As in the core study: a user-supplied Refraction TOP sampled at gl_FragCoord * uTDGeneral.viewport.zw. New here: every lookup is an offset from that position, computed by projecting 3D points with the camera's own view-projection, so an unbent ray lands exactly on its own pixel.

role: refract() of the eye vector by the surface normal: the entry refraction.
adaptation: Kept for the entry (enterGlass). Heckel adds refractVec.xy to the screen position after one surface. Here the ray is followed through the glass to an exit point, refracted again there, and continued Scene depth further before it is projected.

role: Chromatic dispersion: one IOR per colour, extra samples per loop to smooth the split; performance warning about loops.
adaptation: Spectrum slices instead of R/G/B or six bands, as in the core study, but each slice is now refracted at both surfaces with its own IOR, and the IOR follows a Cauchy-shaped curve (violet end spreads more). One Refraction TOP read per slice. No per-pixel noise.

role: Saturation by mixing with luminance (0.2125, 0.7154, 0.0721).
adaptation: Unchanged from the core study: applied once to the transmitted light after the loop.

role: Squared Blinn-Phong specular, diffuse and fresnel glow.
adaptation: Unchanged from the core study (highlights(), rim and reflection weight).

role: Backside rendering: render the back side, then the front side with the same material; cites the Codrops multiside refraction article (line 698).
adaptation: Changed purpose: the back side is rendered as data, not shaded. render_back stores the far side's outward normal (rgb) and eye distance (alpha) in one RGBA 32-bit float target; the front pass marches to the exit, refracts a second time and detects total internal reflection there.

role: The archived final scene (scene9), fragment shader string: the 16-sample loop over six IORs (LOOP = 16 at line 49).
adaptation: Read for the loop structure; no lines copied. Its single refraction per side is replaced by two refractions per slice in one material.

role: The same file's App code: useFrame renders the scene into backRenderTarget with the mesh hidden (257-258), switches the mesh to THREE.BackSide (261), renders into mainRenderTarget (265-266), then back to THREE.FrontSide (269).
adaptation: Read for the back-then-front render order behind the optional back-face pass; no lines copied. Here the back pass stores normals and distances instead of a shaded back side.

role: Choosing an approximation instead of ray tracing; converging rays give brighter caustics, diverging rays dimmer.
adaptation: Motivates the caustic glow and the stated limits: a closed-form estimate, not a light simulation.

role: Rendering a mesh's normals (back side) into a render target with a dedicated material, so another shader can read them.
adaptation: The same move for the back-face pass: material_back swaps in as the Render TOP's override material and writes normals (plus distance) instead of colour. World-space, signed, float; not packed as normal * 0.5 + 0.5.

role: Caustic intensity as the ratio of a light bundle's area before and after refraction (screen derivatives), then clamp and square.
adaptation: Evaluated in closed form for a ball lens instead of with dFdx/dFdy: the bundle's angular radius on the far wall is |2 - n| / n, and the brightness scales with the area ratio (1/9) / radius^2, capped at 4. No derivatives, so no 2x2-pixel blocks.

role: Chromatic aberration on the caustic pattern, smoothed with a per-pixel random offset.
adaptation: Not ported: the brief rules out dithering. Colour edges come from the per-slice IOR inside causticGlow() instead.

role: Sampling a render target with screen coordinates (gl_FragCoord / resolution) instead of UVs.
adaptation: screenUV() from gl_FragCoord and uTDGeneral.viewport, as in the core study.

source_id: codrops: Real-time Multiside Refraction in Three Steps (Jesper Vos, 2019)
kind: external, cited by Heckel (refraction article line 698)
role: Back faces' world normals rendered to a texture first, then used by the front-face refraction shader.
adaptation: Same storage idea. The article blends the back normal into the front one with a weight (per search summaries; the page returned 403 to our fetcher); this study refracts a second time at the measured exit instead.

source_id: Wyman, C. 2005. An Approximate Image-Space Approach for Interactive Refraction. ACM SIGGRAPH 2005 (ACM Transactions on Graphics 24(3)).
role: Refraction through two surfaces in image space using a separate pass for the back-most surface's depth and normals.
adaptation: Credited as the original research behind two-surface image-space refraction. Worked from published summaries, not the paper's full text. The distance estimate here (two secant corrections against the stored eye distance) and the ball-plus-tilt fallback are this study's own. DOI as listed by research indexes (researchr, bohrium); the ACM Digital Library page was not opened.

role: GLSL MAT contract (read 2026-11-01, page oldid 38399).
adaptation: TDDeform/TDDeformNorm/TDWorldToProj; TDCameraIndex is vertex-only so it is passed as a flat varying; uTDGeneral.viewport = (x, y, 1/w, 1/h); TDOutputSwizzle on every colour written. Multiple render targets: outputs declared as fragColor[TD_NUM_COLOR_BUFFERS], set from the Render TOP's # of Color Buffers; writing beyond the provided buffers can corrupt or crash the GPU. Compared in decisions.json; not used.

role: Render TOP parameters (read 2026-11-01, page oldid 36456).
adaptation: numcolorbufs (# of Color Buffers, left at 1), format rgba32float (32-bit float RGBA), overridemat, antialias aa1, bgcolor alpha 0.

role: Selecting one colour buffer of a Render TOP (read 2026-11-01, page oldid 23988, last edited 2021).
adaptation: Parameters top and colorbufindex. Not needed with the single packed target; the page does not state the index base.

role: Snell's law in vector form, the Fresnel equations for unpolarised light, the critical angle sin(a) = 1 / n, Cauchy's dispersion law n = A + B / wavelength^2, and the paraxial focal length of a ball lens f = n R / (2 (n - 1)).
adaptation: Implemented in leaveGlass(), sliceIor() and causticGlow(); the property tests recompute Snell, Fresnel and the Cauchy curve independently in JavaScript.
